findings.explanation: Carried forward from the previous ai-findings.json review. rotation_period is now "7776000s" (90 days), matching the standard used across the author's other modules — resolved by commit 785525a.

findings.explanation: google_storage_bucket.code and google_storage_bucket.logs both set encryption.default_kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name, and google_storage_bucket_object.code_package sets kms_key_name = var.kms_key_name — all three resolve to google_kms_crypto_key.appengine_key via the example's module call. Setting these attributes only tells GCS which key to use; it does not grant access. GCP requires the GCS service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gs-project-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key before the bucket or object can actually be created/written — nowhere in this repo is a google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member/_binding granting that role on this key. As configured, applying this example will fail with a Cloud KMS permission error on the first bucket/object write. Holden's deterministic engine doesn't catch this today, but the identical pattern is already codified for other services (HLD_GCP_448 for Cloud Run CMEK, HLD_GCP_453 for Cloud SQL CMEK) and a GCS-specific version (HLD_GCP_456, in the JamesWoolfenden/holden fork at policies/gcp/storage/bucket-cmek-service-agent-iam.yaml) already exists but is not yet in this project's active policy set (.holden/policies/) nor in the installed holden binary's built-in catalog (925 policies, no HLD_GCP_456) — so the gap in the actual repo isn't visible in this scan's 0-finding result.
findings.title: GCS buckets and objects reference a CMEK, but the GCS service agent is never granted decrypt/encrypt access to that key

findings.explanation: google_app_engine_firewall_rule.allow (priority 1000) permits var.allowed_source_range, set in examplea.auto.tfvars to "10.0.0.0/8" — a private, non-routable range. google_app_engine_firewall_rule.default_deny (priority 2147483647, the required catch-all) denies source_range "*". App Engine firewall rules match the request's apparent public source IP; nothing in this repo configures a Serverless VPC Access connector or internal-only ingress that would make a real client appear to originate from a private range. With no other route to match the allow rule, every genuine internet client falls through to the deny-all rule and the app becomes completely unreachable — the opposite of the "Allow traffic from the trusted source range" comment's intent. This composition (an allow rule whose range can structurally never match combined with a deny-all default) is invisible to a single-resource rule engine.
findings.remediation: If public access is intended, set allowed_source_range to the actual public CIDR(s) that should reach the app (e.g. a partner's egress IP range or an external load balancer's IP). If internal-only access is intended, wire up a Serverless VPC Access connector / internal ingress path so requests genuinely arrive from the private range being allow-listed — this repo currently configures neither.
findings.title: App Engine firewall allow-rule uses a private RFC1918 source range, so with the default-deny catch-all every real internet client is blocked

Also imported into this project's .holden/policies/ and confirmed passing (10.0.0.0/8 is a private range, not the literal wildcard this policy scopes to).
suggested_policies.rationale: google_app_engine_firewall_rule has zero existing holden policy coverage (coverage_by_type is empty for this resource type). App Engine allows all traffic by default when no firewall rules exist, so an ALLOW rule with an unrestricted source_range ("*" or "0.0.0.0/0") provides no access control while making the configuration look deliberately restricted — the same risk pattern as an open security group ingress rule, just for App Engine's own firewall. This does not apply to DENY rules, which legitimately use "*" as the required catch-all default (priority 2147483647).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_457
name: App Engine firewall allow rules must not permit unrestricted source ranges
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  google_app_engine_firewall_rule resources with action = "ALLOW" and
  source_range set to "*" or "0.0.0.0/0" grant every client on the internet
  access. App Engine already allows all traffic by default when no firewall
  rules are defined at all, so an explicit unrestricted ALLOW rule adds no
  protection while making the configuration appear intentionally scoped. This
  check only applies to ALLOW rules — DENY rules legitimately use "*" as the
  required default catch-all (typically at priority 2147483647).
remediation: |
  Scope ALLOW rules to a specific CIDR range instead of allowing all traffic:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_app_engine_firewall_rule" "allow" {
    action       = "ALLOW"
    priority     = 1000
    source_range = "203.0.113.0/24"
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_app_engine_firewall_rule:
    if_equals:
      path: action
      value: ALLOW
      then:
        path: source_range
        not_one_of:
          - "*"
          - "0.0.0.0/0"
